request.spec:
The sheet's due-total and the sheet's overdue-total (wherever they show: the totals row, the
header, the TOTALS line) now leave out the single highest and the single lowest person's figure
when three or more people have a figure (a due-total of n/a is no figure; an overdue-total is
always a figure). Per-person figures, per-grade and per-period totals, backing and the claimed
total are not trimmed.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The sheet's due-total and the sheet's overdue-total (wherever they show: the totals row, the
header, the TOTALS line) now leave out the single highest and the single lowest person's figure
when three or more people have a figure (a due-total of n/a is no figure; an overdue-total is
always a figure). Per-person figures, per-grade and per-period totals, backing and the claimed
total are not trimmed.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The sheet's due-total and overdue-total now leave out the single highest and the single lowest person's figure when three or more people have one. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests.

**On screen** (totals row and header):
- `features/rates/api.ts`: a new `trimmedSum` helper adds up the figures, skipping n/a ones, and drops the top and bottom figure when there are three or more.
- `features/rates/DueTotal.tsx`: the sheet due-total now uses `trimmedSum` over each person's due-total.
- `features/rates/Overdue.tsx`: the sheet overdue-total used to add up all overdue claims in one go. It now works out each person's overdue-total first, then applies `trimmedSum`. A person with nothing overdue counts as 0.00, so they're still a figure. The overdue count isn't trimmed.

**Audit file** (TOTALS line):
- `rollup/Rollup.java`: the sheet due- and overdue-totals use the same trimming. TOTALS is only written when a total actually changes, so a change that leaves the trimmed totals the same writes no TOTALS line. One step in the test relies on this: setting the cap writes a line for Ben but no TOTALS line.

Per-person figures, per-grade and per-period totals, backing and the claimed total are unchanged.
